newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt opposition blames Israel for Sudan conflict.
newsitem.headline: Egypt opposition blames Israel for Sudan conflict.

text.p: Egypt's mainstream opposition parties have sided with the Sudanese government by accusing Israel and other "external powers" of being behind the fighting on Sudan's eastern borders.
"What is going on in Sudan is an international plot," columnist Mohamed Abu el-Futuh wrote in the Islamist Labour party's newspaper al-Shaab on Tuesday.
"Sudan is the enemy of the United States, the Zionist entity (Israel), (Eritrean Presdient) Isayas Afewerki -- that Israeli agent -- and of Ethiopia and others who are against Islam."

Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir has said Ethiopian and Eritrean troops, with a little help from Israel, are behind the fighting in the east, which started nine days ago. He also said both countries were recruiting Sudanese rebels to battle with them.
Eritrea and Ethiopia, which allow Sudanese opposition groups to operate on their territory, deny being involved in the fighting.

The Sudanese opposition and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak have scoffed at Bashir's comments, saying no foreign troops have entered Sudan. Mubarak also said Egypt would not intervene in what he called an internal issue.

But the Egyptian opposition, which has a minority in parliament and very little influence on matters of state, held a rally to support the Sudanese government and cautioned Mubarak that any plot against Sudan would affect Egypt.

"Sudan is facing a great conspiracy to separate its south from its north...Egypt must take a stand to end the bloodshed because it will jeopardise the Nile which provides us with most of our water," said Liberal party leader Mostafa Kamal Murad.

Egypt does not wholeheartedly approve of the Sudanese opposition but its relations with Sudan's Islamist government have been strained for a while, especially after gunmen tried to kill Mubarak in Ethiopia in 1995. Egypt says Sudan is sheltering the three men. Khartoum denies the charges.

Mamoun el-Hodeibi, spokesman for the outlawed and influential Moslem Brotherhood group which is seeking to transform Egypt into a strict Islamic country, said the government's stand was illogical and that it should bolster the Sudanese government.
"This is a plot against Islam and a threat to Egypt's security as Sudan is our neighbour, so how can we not interfere?" Hodeibi said.
"We must not allow those Israeli-led leaders in Eritrea and Ethiopia to take over Sudan and threaten our Nile resources."
Jordan, Yemen, Iraq and Iran also back Sudan and have called on other Arab countries to help end the conflict.
